decisions.title: Modular monolith and local JSON protocol
decisions.context: The server is a Python 3.12 FastAPI application with HTTP, WebSocket, services, repositories, and a 20 Hz match loop.
decisions.problem: The reconstruction needs one place for account, lobby, and match behavior without treating the wire format as an official client protocol.
options_considered: Split services into separate deployable processes now
Keep a modular monolith and a project-specific JSON protocol
decisions.chosen_solution: Keep the modular monolith. HTTP and WebSocket code call services. Services call repositories. The match loop keeps positions in memory.
decisions.reason: This is the recorded architecture in docs/engineering/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md.
decisions.consequences: Official Rules of Survival packet formats stay out of scope. Changing the protocol or the process split needs a new decision record.

decisions.title: Account identity and hashed session storage
decisions.context: Players need a login row and one profile. Sessions are stored on the server.
decisions.problem: Response schemas must not expose password or token secrets.
options_considered: Store Argon2 password hashes and SHA-256 session token hashes
decisions.chosen_solution: accounts is the login row and the JWT subject. players is one profile per account. Passwords use Argon2. Session tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and omitted from response schemas.
decisions.reason: This is the recorded identity decision.
decisions.consequences: Logout, if added, must revoke the stored hash. RO-009 still has to review the implementation.

decisions.title: UUID keys and portable JSON
decisions.context: Development uses SQLite and the production layout expects PostgreSQL.
decisions.problem: One migration has to serve both databases.
decisions.chosen_solution: Primary keys are UUID strings. JSON columns use PortableJSON. The Python attribute for JSON payloads is details. Relationships use lazy=raise.
decisions.reason: This is the recorded portability decision.
decisions.consequences: A skipped PostgreSQL test does not prove the production path. Do not add a second incompatible key style without a new decision.

decisions.title: Preserve legacy player rows
decisions.context: An older players table existed before the normalized schema.
decisions.problem: The new schema must not destroy the old rows during upgrade.
options_considered: Drop the old table during upgrade
Rename it to legacy_players and copy rows
decisions.chosen_solution: Revision 93510e8bf194 renames players to legacy_players, creates the new tables, and copies rows. Upgrade does not drop the legacy table.
decisions.reason: Player-owned rows are protected. Downgrade is only for a disposable database.
decisions.consequences: Do not rewrite this applied revision. Do not delete legacy_players.

decisions.title: Management registries are the project record
decisions.context: The reconstruction runs across many Cursor sessions. Conversation history is not a durable project record.
decisions.problem: Research, implementation, tests, compatibility, and ownership need a record that survives a new session.
options_considered: Keep append-only JSON registries for tasks, discoveries, compatibility, checkpoints, and changelog
decisions.chosen_solution: The JSON files in .cursor/management are the source of truth. The CTO is the only role that changes task assignment or status. Checkpoints and released changelog rows are append-only.
decisions.reason: A later session must be able to resume from files and command evidence.
decisions.consequences: File existence does not change task status. Specialists do not edit the registries. The registries are not the game database.

decisions.title: Local tests do not prove original compatibility
decisions.context: RO-020 recorded 43 server functions. RO-028 reviewed them.
decisions.problem: A passing test of this server can be mistaken for a match to original Rules of Survival.
options_considered: Treat a passing local test as compatible
Keep implementation, test, and original compatibility as separate fields
decisions.chosen_solution: compatibility_status stays unknown unless an authorized original reference is cited and a comparison passed. Research notes must separate observed fact, interpretation, and hypothesis.
decisions.reason: No authorized original specification is in this repository. DIS-0001 records that fact.
decisions.consequences: Do not mark a feature compatible from app tests alone. Do not invent weapon stats, maps, or packet formats.

decisions.title: Enforce stored sessions and separate readiness
decisions.context: Login stored a session hash that HTTP and WebSocket did not read. GET /health returns a fixed liveness body.
decisions.problem: Revocation could not take effect, and a database check could not be added without changing that body.
options_considered: Add a WebSocket logout message and change the health body
Check the stored hash on both existing entry points and add GET /ready
decisions.chosen_solution: POST /api/v1/auth/logout revokes one hash. HTTP and WebSocket reject a missing, revoked, or expired row. GET /health stays unchanged. GET /ready runs SELECT 1.
decisions.reason: RO-038 approved that boundary. It keeps Argon2, JWT expiration checks, and the current client protocol.
decisions.consequences: Other sessions stay valid. Original logout behavior stays unknown. PostgreSQL execution remains RO-045.

decisions.title: Stored match records stay separate from the live match
decisions.context: The live match list and the stored match table use different identifiers.
decisions.problem: One route path would make cancel and finalize apply to the wrong match.
decisions.chosen_solution: Live snapshots stay on /matches. Stored create, join, cancel, and finalize use /match-records.
decisions.reason: The tick loop does not write SQL. The stored row is a separate lifecycle.
decisions.consequences: A stored cancel does not stop an in-memory match. Original matchmaking stays unknown.
